data.narrative:
Paradromics is a Series B biotech company founded by Matt Angle, Edmund Huber, and Andreas Schaefer, having raised approximately $90–120M in equity plus ~$18M in non-dilutive NIH/DARPA funding. The valuation analysis triangulates across a peer universe of 8 private and 3 public companies in Biotech & Health, including Series B and C stage comparables such as Eikon Therapeutics ($539M), Chai Discovery ($3.8B), Colossal Biosciences ($10.3B), and New Limit ($3.1B).

Two methods prove applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x multiplier to the $90M raised proxy, implying a valuation of $171M. Peer-median analysis across the four core comparables yields a median valuation of $3.5B, with a range from $539M to $10.3B. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples (6.2x median across RXRX, TEM, and ONT.L) cannot be applied due to absence of disclosed revenue figures for the target. The wide dispersion in peer valuations reflects heterogeneity in technology maturity, capital efficiency, and stage progression within the biotech sector.

Triangulation of applicable methods supports a range of $145M (low) to $4.0B (high), with a median of $1.8B. The substantial gap between stage-progression and peer-median results reflects tension between early-stage capital multiples and the elevated valuations commanded by later-stage biotech peers. Key uncertainties include the timing and structure of the Series B close, clinical or technical inflection points relative to peer benchmarks, and the differentiation value of Paradromics' core technology platform versus the peer set.
